**Verdict: all 3, sequenced. Contractor now, migrate to managed K8s (EKS/GKE/AKS), then hire 1 platform engineer. Don't just re-hire into the same setup, you'd recreate the bus factor of 1.**

**Week 1, before the engineer's last day:**
- Get all credentials: cloud root, cluster-admin kubeconfigs, CI/CD secrets, DNS, registry.
- Find expiry dates for cluster certs (kubeadm default 1 yr) & TLS.
- Verify etcd backups by actually restoring one.
- Record walkthroughs: deploy, rollback, node replacement, upgrade, incident history.
- Offer a paid part-time retainer for 1–2 months.
- Freeze cluster upgrades & infra changes.

**Weeks 1–12, contractor/consultancy:**
- Scope a fixed deliverable: stabilize, migrate to managed control plane, put everything in IaC/GitOps, write runbooks.
- Avoid open-ended staff augmentation.
- Pair 2 of your engineers w/ them, so knowledge lands in-house.

**Why migrate:**
- The control plane (etcd, upgrades, certs, API server HA) is the riskiest part to run w/o an expert.
- Managed K8s removes it for approx. $75/mo per cluster.
- Your manifests, Helm charts & CI mostly carry over.
- Main work: networking, ingress, storage, IAM.

**Don't move to PaaS/serverless (ECS, Cloud Run) now:** re-platforming 40 services w/ no ops expertise is too much risk. Revisit later.

**Hire, start now (takes 2–4 months):**
- 1 platform-minded engineer, to own the managed setup.
- Easier to fill than "run bare K8s alone".
- Keep the 2 paired engineers as backup on-call.

**Caveats that change this:**
- On-prem/bare metal: managed isn't a quick swap. Use a longer contractor engagement, or evaluate a cloud move separately.
- Already on a cloud but self-managing (kops/kubeadm on VMs): the easiest case, same plan.
